segments.narration: Australia declared war on birds and lost. November 1932, Western Australia, and the enemy was twenty thousand emus.
The birds were flattening wheat that soldier-settlers had been given after the First World War. The farmers asked for machine guns.
They got them. Two Lewis guns, ten thousand rounds, and a major to run the operation.
Emus do not stand still. They split into small groups, ran at fifty kilometres an hour, and absorbed hits that should have dropped them.
The final count was under a thousand birds for nearly ten thousand rounds. The operation was quietly dropped and fences were built instead.
